title: Fresh-agent scenarios and two-part field reports

nodes.summary: Versioned scenario packages run by a fresh, unscripted agent
nodes.detail: Each scenario packages a synthetic seeded KB, fixed plugin sources and inputs, a user-level task, declared starting knowledge/tools, observable outcome checks and a reflection prompt. A fresh agent without implementation context gets the task and normal product discovery, never a tool-name script or the evaluator's checklist.

realised.evidence: Only architecture/field-experience scenario/report templates exist; the README states they are 'not an implemented harness or evidence that a scenario has run'

nodes.summary: Optional MCP adapter-boundary instrumentation as a test observer
nodes.detail: Runs go through the real MCP adapter, instrumenting discovery and calls with operation IDs, timing, status, selected snapshot/candidate and response volume, plus CLI/file-edit fallbacks and human intervention. Instrumentation is an optional observer, not a KB effect or mandatory production provenance ledger.

realised.evidence: No MCP telemetry observer in the host; only opt-in CLI phase timings (PR #134), which are not this instrumentation

nodes.summary: Two-part field reports: observed outcome plus agent's own account
nodes.detail: The agent's experience account is collected before it sees the evaluator's interpretation, results are inspected independently, and the report pairs trace/outcome with experience plus reviewer synthesis. Hidden chain-of-thought is never requested.

realised.evidence: report-template.md encodes the shape but no field report has been produced

nodes.summary: Labelled access conditions, recorded run identity, repeats, visible failures
nodes.detail: Natural-access and MCP-only probe runs are labelled; exact build, scenario revision, model/harness/config, prompt, tool catalog and cache state are recorded. Important comparisons repeat, and partial, failed, cancelled or assisted runs stay visible.

realised.evidence: No runs exist to which the discipline applies

nodes.summary: Scenarios cover installation, schema authoring and labelled web handoffs
nodes.detail: Scenarios include agent-driven install/readiness and opening a KB for a human (ADR 0025), Haskell schema-authoring ergonomics without reopening the authority decision, and web/human handoffs where any agent-simulated human is labelled and cannot establish human usability.

realised.evidence: No scenarios of any kind have been run

editorial.note: Front-matter/title reformat and removal of the Proposed status line; content unchanged

notes: The lane is pure method: founded at seq 1 and only reformatted at seq 143, and none of it is realised. The repo carries scenario and report templates (architecture/field-experience/) that explicitly disclaim being a harness or evidence of a run, and PROJECT-PRACTICES defers field runs until the relevant product paths exist. It is the clearest case of spec far ahead of code; the nearest related code (opt-in CLI phase timings, PR #134) is not the MCP-boundary observer described here. The 'Experiment discipline' section was treated as decision content (it is not Context/Consequences/Verification) and split into run discipline vs scenario coverage.
